rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted revision fd6b0bc7 (installed chunked-stem bundle trial-3c4e540078-param-d377cbf2, measured 204,905,472 B against the 281,975,808 B original; project_measurement noise_bounds 0). The operative measured fact from previous-feedback is the stem_chunk plateau: parameter search measured 204,905,472 B at stem_chunk=4 AND at 8 (207,002,624 B at 16), so the stem is no longer the binding site; the arithmetic that reproduces all three points puts the peak in the encoder frame: persistent live 67,831,968 B (params 46,758,048 + pixels 19,267,584 + images 1,806,336) plus the (32,64,56,56) embedding_output pinned for the whole encoder plus ~3 more transient (32,64,56,56) buffers during stage 0/1 (~4x25,690,112 B) plus cudnn workspace/allocator residue. This attempt therefore moves the boundary to the region root ResNetModel.forward (call 8fbf233236c985c7650ea8e4) and replaces it with a micro-batched executor: slice the GPU-resident (32,3,224,224) FP32 contiguous input into model_chunk batches, per chunk call the current parent callables through context.references (embedder 683c822136ed7958f3e9ba44, encoder 29488c4be587b49a7875c533 with output_hidden_states=False/return_dict=True exactly as the parent resolves and observes, pooler 61beb430723e6c6d4991e78c), narrow-copy each chunk's (c,512,7,7) last_hidden_state and (c,512,1,1) pooled output into preallocated full-batch outputs, and return BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndNoAttention with unchanged shapes/fields so the untouched classifier consumes outputs.pooler_output identically. Every op in the region is per-sample (3x3/1x1 conv windows, eval-mode BN with frozen running stats, out-of-place ReLU, in-block residual add_, per-sample max/adaptive-average pooling; transformers 5.16.1 ResNetModel.forward verified in the worker venv to be exactly embedder -> encoder -> pooler -> this output object), so chunked execution is the identical computation per image - the same property the evaluator already accepted for the stem chunk. Composition decision, stated against the installed bundle's actual bytes: the accepted stem bundle's dispatch guard matches only its declared full-batch signature (inputs/previous-candidate/targets.json declares args (32,3,224,224) float32 cuda contiguous, kwargs {} for 683c822136ed7958f3e9ba44), and the binding contract's dispatch falls back to the original parent forward on any other signature; the current candidate_diagnostics record corroborates that the stem callable ran only on full-batch calls (counts 683c822136ed7958f3e9ba44=2 over 2 diagnostic steps, zero fallbacks). Per-chunk embedder calls with (8,3,224,224) therefore execute the original parent stem (numerically identical per sample) but cannot increment the inherited bundle's required coverage counter, which the evaluator makes mandatory for every installed bundle. Following the binding contract ('All inherited required calls remain mandatory unless the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced'), this proposal explicitly replaces the earlier whole bundle trial-3c4e540078-param-d377cbf2 and preserves its needed behavior itself: model-level chunking keeps stem transients at chunk size (the accepted bundle's entire memory effect) and extends the same property to the encoder and pooler phases, so the replaced bundle's boundary is not left unowned. Memory expectation (hypothesis to be measured, derived from the calibration above, not an observed fact): no full-batch (32,64,56,56) tensor is ever allocated; predicted per-forward peak at model_chunk=8 is roughly 67.8 MB persistent + 3.3 MB preallocated outputs + ~52-58 MB chunk-8 stem conv/BN coexistence + chunk-sized stage-0 transients + cudnn workspace, i.e. ~130-160 MB, and ~105-135 MB at model_chunk=4; model_chunk=16 (~180-195 MB) is retained as a throughput-safe retreat point. Throughput expectation: the accepted stem candidate at chunk 8 measured 4.00 ms vs the 4.24 ms original (gate 7174.15 img/s, original 7551.73) despite 4x stem launches, because chunk-8 scudnn convolutions stay fully occupied (grid 784); the residual risk is quadrupled launch counts of the small stage-2/3 kernels, which the images_per_second >= 0.95x gate and the model_chunk parameter search police. Previous feedback changes this attempt precisely by locating the remaining peak outside the stem and by proving the references/guard composition style; no failed path needs repair (decision.accepted true, empty reasons, no candidate_diagnostics events).

setup_work.build_time: build(context) only resolves the parent callables from context.references/context.modules and reads model metadata (embedder.num_channels, config.output_hidden_states/return_dict defaults). No CUDA tensor is created, no weights are transformed or repacked, no CUDA Graph is captured, no fixture-dependent output is cached, and module import performs no CUDA initialization; the workload executes fully on each invocation from the current pixel_values.
setup_work.runtime_allocations: Per forward the replacement allocates exactly two full-batch output buffers after the first chunk returns: last_hidden_state (32,512,7,7) FP32 = 3,211,264 B and pooler_output (32,512,1,1) FP32 = 65,536 B, plus chunk-sized transients owned by the parent callables (chunk/32 of the corresponding full-batch activation sizes). Chunk slice views of the input allocate nothing.
setup_work.retained_pools: No CUDA Graph pool and no persistent cache is retained by this candidate; installation adds no setup allocation (the framework records installation allocation separately in its setup receipts).
setup_work.memory_scope: The optimized metric is the per-run process-level PyTorch CUDA allocated peak (peak stats reset before each repeat). Reserved-memory pools, lifecycle peaks (which include preparation/installation) and non-PyTorch driver allocations are separate framework counters; nothing here is claimed as a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: cudnn heuristic algorithm selection at chunk batch sizes may differ from batch 32 and change floating-point accumulation order in convolutions; this is the same drift class the evaluator already accepted for the chunked stem, and it is verified by the paired assert_close(atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4) full-logits comparison rather than assumed.

require_exact_top1 compares integer argmax tensors exactly; a near-tie in logits could in principle flip under tiny numerical drift. Expected argmax margins dwarf the noise; validated by the exact-top1 gate in the quality run.

All fallback paths (setup failure, unsupported signature/kwargs, grad-enabled call, non-CUDA/non-FP32/non-contiguous input, channel mismatch, runtime exception) execute the parent reference and are output-identical by construction; the frozen inference workload matches the observed signature so the chunked path is the one exercised and counted.

Autograd/training semantics are not exercised by the frozen inference workload; the replacement falls back to the parent whenever gradients are enabled instead of claiming unverified autograd equivalence.

Numerical policies are untouched: no TF32, cudnn.benchmark stays False, FP32 weights and activations, no in-place rewrite of any parent tensor (assembly writes only into the candidate-owned preallocated outputs); the returned last_hidden_state/pooler_output are fresh buffers exactly as the parent's are.

The earlier chunked-stem bundle is explicitly replaced; its boundary behavior (chunk-sized stem transients) is preserved and subsumed by model-level chunking, and every in-region descendant call still executes (per chunk), so no consumer of an eliminated call exists.

params.name: model_chunk
params.description: Images per model-level batch chunk. Smaller chunks shrink every per-phase transient to chunk/32 of the full-batch size (stem conv/BN coexistence, stage-0/1 activation stack) at the cost of more kernel launches across the ~4 ms forward; 8 is the default, 16 is the throughput-safe retreat point. The chunk never changes batch, sampling, data, dtype or output semantics; N <= model_chunk degrades to a single parent-equivalent chunk.
